newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat up as KCBT rallies on crop loss woes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat up as KCBT rallies on crop loss woes.

text.p: CBOT wheat turned higher and nearly every contract was in fast dealings at midsession with escalating concerns about the degree of crop damage over the weekend in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region plus EU crop concerns boosting prices, traders said.
Traders said there still were some estimates that up to 200 million bushels of wheat were lost last weekend during freezing weather in key U.S. hard red winter wheat growing areas.
They also cited Thursday's decision by the EU to halt its weekly export tender for wheat as stirring concern.
"There are all kind of horror stories and they pulled some rain out of Europe. All of a sudden we've gone from bearish to bullish in a week," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
At 1056 CDT, wheat was 2-3/4 to six cents per bushel higher, with May up 3-1/4 at $4.28-1/2. July was up five at $4.36.
